newsitem.title: ARGENTINA: Argentine stocks pare gains, seen pausing.
newsitem.headline: Argentine stocks pare gains, seen pausing.

text.p: Argentina's bolsa pushed higher for the seventh consecutive session Friday but stocks slipped off their highs at the close as profit-taking capped a bullish week, dealers said.

"Gains were clearly driven by Wall Street today," said Adolfo Adorno at Agra traders. "The market is still firm based on prospects for a long-term debt buyback scheme, which is luring foreign buyers, but until this news is confirmed we could start to see some volatility."
The blue-chip MerVal index .MERV closed up 0.4 percent at 577.62 against a session high of 581.15.
The MerVal amassed gains of 4.0 percent in the week and 6.1 percent in the past seven sessions, and now stands at its highest point in three months.
"Stocks are heading for some profit-taking because at these prices most of the good local news has been discounted," said Dario Lizzano at brokers Rio Valores.
Traders said the markets would stay tuned for any fresh speculation surrounding the Brady buyback, although Economy Minister Roque Fernandez said recently no swap was imminent.
"It seems Fernandez will hold out for the best possible market conditions to get a good rate," said Adorno.
The bolsa will also continue to track Wall Street, which soared Friday as the U.S. long bond yield tumbled to 6.75 percent from 6.83 percent on a very weak jobs report.
Local debate on labor reforms was another key factor for the markets.

"Investors are concerned that spreading trade union protests may undermine the labor bill sent Monday to Congress, but so far (President Carlos) Menem has not wavered and looks ready to face the unions head-on," said Adorno.
In the session the broad market rose 0.3 percent, with winners beating losers 34 to 13 and 22 issues closing flat.
In the session floor volume rose marginally to 24.1 million pesos, while over-the-counter deals swelled to 175 million pesos from 128 million Thursday.
Best main-tier performers were carmaker Sevel, real estate developer Irsa and holding company Comercial del Plata, which rose 3.8 percent, 3.3 percent and 2.4 percent, respectively.

Losers were led by construction stock Polledo, which dropped 2.9 percent, steelmaker Siderca, which shed 2.0 percent, and Telecom, which lost 1.6 percent after shooting up 6.0 percent in the previous two sessions.
